children: Oil futures give back some gains after rising to four-month highs on extended risks to supply routes out of the Middle East. "We're seeing the markets pricing in the higher risk associated with beliefs that the conflict could continue longer," says Angie Gildea, global head of oil and gas at KPMG. Damage to the Saudi pipeline, drawdowns in SPRinventories and increased Chinese buying "is factoring into the pricing." SPR withdrawals can't go on forever, "so at some point we get into some real challenges," Gildea adds. WTI settles down 3.2% at $102.43 a barrel and Brent falls 2.7% to $105.83. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
